title: repair_mesh node: weld seams, orient, split non-manifold edges, drop degenerates, classify shells, fill small holes
description:
Topological repair for generated scans so the quad-layout pipeline never runs on a broken shell. Measured on IMG_4109.glb by CRAW-2: 622,652 V / 936,035 F raw with 298,169 fake boundary edges from UV-seam vertex duplication (154,302 duplicate positions); welded by exact position it has 943 real boundary edges, 125 non-manifold edges, 33 inconsistently oriented edges, 2 degenerate faces and 14 edge-connected shells (919,762 / 15,118 / 214 / ... / 1 faces). CRAW-21 and CRAW-3 hit the same seam split. Node `repair_mesh(geometry, weld_epsilon=0, max_hole_edges, min_shell_faces, strict)` in nodes/modifier, data/algorithm split: `MeshRepairReport` (public int counts per class, per-shell face counts and containment, per-hole edge counts, what was left open) and `MeshRepair` stages in this order: (1) weld by exact position (epsilon optional) keeping a vertex-to-original map so per-vertex slots (TextureCoordinates UV, tags) are carried per corner or re-indexed, never silently fused -- coordinate with CRAW-3's merge_by_distance weld map; (2) orient by BFS from the largest face, reporting Mobius contradictions as non-manifold; (3) split non-manifold edges by duplicating the edge and its vertices per face-fan pair, deleting nothing; (4) degenerate faces: collapse the shortest edge when neighbours stay valid, else delete and treat the slit as a hole; (5) shells: classify by face count and ray-parity containment (enclosed bubble vs external fragment), drop only debris below min_shell_faces or enclosed, report the rest (the 15k-face shell must be inspected, not dropped); (6) holes: loops with at most max_hole_edges get minimum-area triangulation then refinement and fairing (Liepa 2003), larger loops stay open and are reported (the missing back side is not repairable; CRAW-24 flags it). strict=true fails evaluation with the report when anything was left open or dropped. Never decimates: no surface the scan has is removed except degenerate faces and debris shells. Slivers are out of scope (quality, not topology; see CRAW-27). Wire the node into the CRAW-2 benchmark and the mesh-viewer load path (optional, off by default) replacing the throwaway weld in CrawfishQuadLayoutBenchmark.

Correction: the sliver reference above should not point at CRAW-27 (that is the singular-system diagnosis ticket). Sliver repair by edge flips has no ticket yet; it needs a user ruling on flips (vertex-preserving) versus collapses (decimation) and should be created once CRAW-27's diagnosis says slivers are the cause.

Ruling 2026-09-06: the seam weld (stage 1) is done by the glTF loader on import (CRAW-12), so repair_mesh only needs an epsilon weld for genuinely near-coincident vertices; per-corner UVs survive welds without a map.

Ruling 2026-09-06: fill ALL holes. The 'missing back side' in the ticket was a misreading: Trellis produces a poor but closed back surface, not an opening, so no hole on these scans is a gap to preserve. Remove the idea that large loops are left open; max_hole_edges becomes a safety cap only (default large, e.g. 4096) and the four remaining IMG_4109 loops (87/86/74/65 edges) get filled and faired like the rest. strict mode then fails only on holes above the safety cap and on Mobius contradictions, not on debris drops.
definition-of-done: 1. Unit (procedural, no files): seam-split square welds to 4 vertices with UVs intact per corner; a fin on a cube becomes a separate boundary flap; a Mobius strip is reported not silently oriented; a sphere with an interior bubble drops the bubble and keeps the sphere; a 6-edge hole is filled and faired. 2. IMG_4109.glb repairs to one main shell with a report listing every class count; strict mode fails only on the large back-side openings, which are listed with their edge counts. 3. CRAW-2 benchmark uses the node and its load/repair rows match the previous throwaway numbers within 1%. 4. Report output is byte-stable across runs. 5. Launch entry 'CRAW-26: Mesh Viewer (repaired crawfish scan)' shows the repaired scan with boundary loops highlighted; screenshot under tmp/. 6. Build checkstyle-green; no unit test loads a mesh file.
testing-plan: 1. Procedural fixtures for each defect class. 2. run-scene on IMG_4109.glb with repair on, ixdar-cli mesh-state shows the report. 3. Re-run CrawfishQuadLayoutBenchmark load/repair stages.
todos: MeshRepairReport value + MeshRepair stages 1-6 with reusable buffers
Weld keeps vertex-to-original map; slot carry rules for _uv and _tags
Replace the benchmark's throwaway weld with the node
Unit fixtures: seam-split square, fin, Mobius strip, bubble-in-sphere, small hole
Fill the four remaining IMG_4109 holes; raise max_hole_edges to a safety cap; strict ignores debris drops
unknowns: Whether the 15,118-face second shell of IMG_4109 is an interior bubble or a detached external part; the containment test decides, verify visually
Per-corner UV storage vs vertex-to-original map after the weld: which one CRAW-3 and CRAW-14 want
Hole size threshold in edges vs in fraction of local skeleton radius

ANSWERED: the 15,118-face second shell of IMG_4109 is an external detached part, not an interior bubble -- three axis rays from a face centroid cross the other shells an even number of times, so containment is false and repair_mesh keeps it. Still worth one visual confirmation of what that part is (it is roughly 1.6% of the scan).

ANSWERED: per-corner UV storage wins over a vertex-to-original UV map. The loader's CornerUvField survives welds, flips, splits and shell drops with no map at all; the map is only needed for the genuinely per-vertex slots (_tags, _bone_weight_*), and MeshRepair keeps one for those.

ArrayMesh never builds the lazy edge topology its own javadoc promises: topologyReady, halfEdgeTwin, edgeHalfEdge, vertexEdgeOffsets and the rest are declared but nothing ever fills them, and every topology accessor has a stray blank first line where an ensureTopology() call clearly used to sit. So ArrayMesh.edgeCount() is always 0, isBoundaryEdge would NPE, ArrayMeshEngine.deleteEdges early-returns, subdivideQuadsOnce reads srcE=0, and ixdar-cli mesh-state reports every ArrayMesh as closed with zero edges. Out of scope here (repair_mesh sidesteps it by emitting a HalfEdgeMesh) but it needs its own ticket.

strict=true trips on dropped shells as well as open loops, per the ticket's own wording. On IMG_4109 with min_shell_faces=100 that means it reports 4 open loops AND 67 debris shells; only with min_shell_faces=0 does it narrow toward the openings alone (28 enclosed one- and two-face fragments are still dropped). If strict should ignore debris drops and fail only on unrepairable openings, that is a ruling to make.

Fairing is the biharmonic descent x <- x - tau*U(U(x)) on the uniform umbrella with the loop fixed, run 200 iterations at tau=0.05, rather than a direct U^2 solve. Cheap and stable on the small patches the scans produce (the largest filled loop is 59 edges); revisit if a filled patch ever needs to be large.

Hole size is still thresholded in edges, not in a fraction of the local skeleton radius. On IMG_4109 the edge threshold separates cleanly (the four unrepairable openings are 87/86/74/65 edges, the largest filled loop is 59), so there was no pressure to change it.
SUPERSEDED by the 2026-09-06 fill-all-holes ruling: the earlier unknown about strict tripping on debris shell drops is resolved -- drops no longer fail strict, and strict now passes on IMG_4109.
SUPERSEDED: the earlier note that fairing used biharmonic gradient descent no longer applies; it is a direct conjugate-gradient solve with two-ring Dirichlet data.

The hole-fill uses the uniform umbrella, not the cotangent or scale-dependent operator, in both the refinement and the fairing solve. Good enough here (patch interiors match the surrounding crease to within a few degrees), but a cotangent Laplacian is the standard upgrade if a filled patch ever has to carry a quad layout or a texture.

max_hole_edges at its 4096 default is nominal on these scans (the largest loop is 87 edges). The triangulation is cubic in time and quadratic in memory, so a genuinely 4096-edge loop would hang; if a future mesh has one, the DP needs a windowed or hierarchical variant rather than a bigger cap.

repair_mesh is at 1014-1215ms on IMG_4109, not under 1s, and the remaining gap is not in the repair algorithm: assemble takes ~370ms of it and 30 of its 36 profiler samples are HalfEdgeMeshEngine.buildFromIndexedMesh (938k addFaceInternal calls, each clearing and refilling three per-face IntIdLists and appending to a per-vertex one, plus computeNormals at ~70ms). Everything MeshRepair itself does is now ~740ms. Getting under 1s means making that shared builder cheaper, which speeds up every mesh op in the repo and deserves its own ticket -- it is not a repair_mesh change.

MeshRepairReport.unorientedEdgeCount can never be reported non-zero through the node: assemble counts it from the flat arrays but then calls HalfEdgeMeshEngine.buildFromIndexedMesh, whose addFaceInternal throws InvalidMeshTopologyException the moment a directed half-edge is claimed twice, which is exactly what an unoriented edge is. So strict mode's check on it is unreachable -- the build fails first. Either strict should test it before assembling (it already does, but the throw wins) or the field should be documented as an invariant that is always 0 in the output. Needs a ruling.

The epsilon weld now inherits MeshMergeByDistance's semantics rather than its own: clusters are transitive (a chain of within-epsilon vertices fuses end to end) and collapse to the cluster AVERAGE, where the old local weld snapped each vertex to the first representative found. Same answer for exactly-coincident vertices, which is the only case the scans and the fixtures exercise, but a genuinely near-coincident cloud will now move slightly. It is also slower on a large HalfEdgeMesh input, because MeshMergeByDistance routes non-ArrayMesh inputs through the HashMap path rather than its primitive one; weld_epsilon is 0 on the crawfish scans so nothing measures it today.

ixdar-cli multiview renders an all-black 4096x2048 composite for the mesh-viewer scene, while a plain ixdar-cli screenshot of the same live scene renders the mesh correctly. Pre-existing and unrelated to this ticket's changes -- the previous agent's tmp/probe-multiview.png is black too -- but it means the launch-entry evidence is a pair of single-angle screenshots rather than the 8-view grid.
changes-made: MeshRepairReport (public int counts per class; per-shell face-count/contained/kept arrays; per-hole edge-count/filled arrays; byte-stable toText() and summaryLine(); _repair_report slot; open_boundary edge-marks label) in geometry/mesh/data/ops.

MeshRepair (geometry/mesh/data/ops) runs the six stages in ticket order on flat working arrays: optional epsilon weld by spatial hash keeping a vertex-to-original map, slit-face drop, orientation, non-manifold split, degenerate faces, shell classification, hole filling, then compaction.

Orientation is per consistent-component, not per face: components are unioned across edges whose two faces already run opposite, then two-coloured breadth-first from the component of the largest face. A plain face-by-face BFS cascades one contested edge into flipping half the shell -- measured 482,838 flips and 9,728 false Mobius reports on IMG_4109; the component form gives 0 flips and exactly the 33 real contradictions.

Non-manifold split is a union-find over face corners joined only across manifold edges, so each edge-connected fan gets its own vertex copy; nothing is deleted. A face still sharing an edge after that is detached on all three corners and reported (detachedFaceCount, 0 on IMG_4109).

MeshHoleFiller implements Liepa 2003: minimum-area interval DP that refuses chords the mesh already carries, sqrt(2)-density centroid refinement with Delaunay edge flips, then biharmonic (umbrella-squared) fairing of the minted vertices with the loop fixed. Loops over 512 edges are refused outright (the DP is cubic).
repair_mesh node in nodes/modifier with weld_epsilon/max_hole_edges/min_shell_faces/strict, socketDocs, a summary log line and strict-mode failure carrying the full report.

The node outputs a HalfEdgeMesh rather than an ArrayMesh: ArrayMesh never builds its lazy edge topology (see unknowns), so edge ids -- and therefore the open_boundary edge marks, the mesh-viewer overlay and mesh-state's edge/boundary counts -- do not exist on it. Emitting the half-edge mesh is also what the pipeline consumes.

Per-corner _uv is carried through every stage (flips swap corners, splits duplicate them, fills get NaN and are counted in unsetUvCornerCount); _tags and _bone_weight_* are re-indexed through the vertex-to-original map; input _edge_marks are dropped as invalid.
MeshNodeViewerScene.getMeshRepairReport() and a repairReport field in the ui/State mesh section, so ixdar-cli mesh-state prints the whole report.

Unit fixtures (procedural, no files): unit/mesh/MeshRepairTest -- seam-split square welds to 4 with per-corner UVs intact, fin on a cube splits into its own boundary flap (and is dropped as debris at min_shell_faces=2), Mobius strip reports 33-style contradictions instead of being silently oriented, tetrahedron inside an octahedron is dropped by ray parity, six-edge hole is filled and faired while the 18-edge loop stays open, report is byte-stable, strict mode fails and passes.

test/benchmark/CrawfishMeshRepairBenchmark: IMG_4109.glb repairs in 2.6-3.0s. 468,350 V / 936,035 F in, 468,816 V / 937,368 F out. mobius 33, non-manifold edges 158 (127 over-used + the 33), split vertices 396, degenerate 4 (2 slits deleted, 2 zero-area collapsed), 74 shells (919,950 / 15,118 / 214 / 186 / 148 / 128 / 108 kept, 67 debris shells of 177 faces dropped), 74 boundary loops, 70 filled with 1,516 triangles and 352 vertices, 4 left open at 87/86/74/65 edges = the 312 remaining boundary edges.

Launch entry 'CRAW-26: Mesh Viewer (repaired crawfish scan)' plus dsl/crawfish_repaired.dsl; screenshots tmp/craw-26-repaired-crawfish.png and tmp/craw-26-boundary-loops.png (the open loops render amber through the CRAW-21 edge-mark overlay).

RULING 2026-09-06 (fill all holes): Trellis closes the back surface badly rather than leaving it open, so no boundary loop on these scans is a gap to preserve. max_hole_edges is now a safety cap only, default 4096 (was 64); MeshHoleFiller's own ceiling moved 512 -> 4096 to match. All 74 loops on IMG_4109 now fill, including the four at 87/86/74/65 edges.

Fairing replaced: was gradient descent on the biharmonic energy with only the loop fixed, which flattens a patch against the surrounding curvature. Now a direct matrix-free conjugate-gradient solve of the normal equations of min ||U x||^2 over the minted vertices, with BOTH the loop and its surrounding one-ring of surface vertices as Dirichlet data, so the patch leaves the surface along its tangent. MeshHoleFiller gained ringX/ringY/ringZ, ringCount and surfaceEdges for that; MeshRepair.fillLoop gathers them from the working vertex adjacency. The solve converges to a residual of 1e-13 on the largest patch (155 unknowns, 119 ring, 87 loop).

Fill quality measured on the four largest patches, per the ruling: mean dihedral crease across the patch INTERIOR is 11-20deg against 9-19deg for the surrounding surface in the same neighbourhood, so the patch matches local curvature -- it neither bulges nor flattens. The higher rim figure (34-77deg mean) is the fixed scan rim itself: a hole's boundary loop zig-zags, so triangles meeting across it crease regardless of the fill. Close-ups under tmp/craw-26-fill-p1-87edge.png, -p2-65edge, -p3-86edge, -p4-74edge; the only visibly rough spot is a thin web where the fill bridges two nearly-touching surfaces at a claw joint, which is the slot's geometry, not the fairing.

strict mode narrowed: it now fails on boundary loops left open (over the cap or with no valid triangulation) and on orientation contradictions that SURVIVE the split, not on debris or bubble shell drops. Added report.unorientedEdgeCount, measured on the repaired mesh: mobiusEdgeCount counts contradictions in the INPUT (33 on IMG_4109) and the non-manifold split resolves every one, so testing it would have made strict unpassable on this scan. Report gained oversizedHoleCount and unfillableHoleCount so the failure names which kind.

IMG_4109.glb re-run, all holes filled: 468,350 V / 936,035 F in -> 469,131 V / 1,407,453 E / 938,302 F out, boundary edges 0, unoriented edges 0, Euler characteristic -20, repair 3.0s (load 0.13s). 74 loops all filled with 2,450 triangles and 667 minted vertices (was 70 of 74, 1,516 triangles, 352 vertices). Other classes unchanged: mobius 33, non-manifold 158, split vertices 396, degenerate 4, 74 shells with 7 kept and 67 debris shells of 177 faces dropped. HalfEdgeMeshEngine.buildFromIndexedMesh accepts the result and strict mode passes.

Launch-entry screenshot regenerated at tmp/craw-26-repaired-crawfish.png: the open_boundary overlay is empty (0 amber pixels in every view), the mesh viewer reports boundaryEdgeCount 0 and closed=true, and ixdar-cli mesh-state carries the whole report. Unit suite 195 tests with only the pre-existing DenseMeshFewSplitsTest failing; checkstyle green; tools/teavm-build.sh BUILD SUCCESS.

PERF (2026-09-06): repair_mesh on IMG_4109 went 3016ms -> 1014-1215ms (best 1014, mean ~1120 over 6 runs) with the report line and the output fingerprint byte-identical (sha256 7304dc3eb2c971e0fa4ff98216ac7692250042cf4d4da47bff744d867b03f834, V 469131 F 938302, filled=74 open=0 boundaryEdges=0). Profiler total samples 956 -> 441; the old top self-time frames MeshRepair.crossingCount (100, 10.5%), Arrays.binarySearch0 (73, 7.6%) and MeshRepair.outsideSpan (63, 6.6%) are all gone, and G1 dropped from ~17% of samples to under 2%.

Shell containment now runs through TriangleBvh (new, geometry/mesh/data), a bounding-volume tree built once over every alive face with the shell id as its group; a query walks only the nodes the axis ray enters and skips its own group. The old test cast 3 rays per shell against all 936,035 faces for 74 shells (208M triangle tests); the tree makes it 74 x 3 short walks. Node boxes are unioned during the same pass that partitions the parent, and per-triangle boxes are precomputed once, so the build is two passes per level rather than three. Containment results are identical because the box test is exactly conservative: an axis ray's hit point shares the origin's two other coordinates and lies inside the triangle's own box, so no crossing can hide in a pruned node.

The ray-triangle test moved out of MeshRepair into TriangleGeometry (new, geometry/mesh/data) as positiveAxisRayCrosses (axis-span reject then Moller-Trumbore over a flat float[] of positions), which also now carries the triangle area MeshRepair.faceArea used to compute inline. TriangleGeometry follows the CurveGeometry precedent in the same package.

The edge table is built once and reused: an edgesDirty flag makes ensureEdges() rebuild only after a stage that changed the faces, and dropDeadEdgeUses() patches the table in place when a stage only DELETED faces (shell drops, and degenerate deletions when nothing was collapsed) by compacting each edge's use list and dropping the edges left empty. On IMG_4109 that is 4 builds instead of 6.

buildEdges itself is linear: corner uses are counting-sorted into buckets keyed by their lower vertex and each bucket is sorted on (higher vertex, slot), so the distinct edges fall out in key order with no Arrays.binarySearch per use and no global sort of 2.8M longs. Buckets of 16 or fewer use an inline insertion sort. All six working buffers are kept between calls with 2x growth headroom, which is what took G1 from ~17% of samples to under 2%. Byte-identical output: the bucket order (low, then high, then slot) is exactly the old sorted-key order.

Boxed maps are gone from the hot paths. MeshRepair.fillLoop's two HashMap<Integer,Integer> (loop-local and ring-local index) are now int[] scratch fields indexed by working vertex, filled and reset per loop. The weld's HashMap<Long,Integer> spatial-hash cell table went with the weld itself (see the MeshMergeByDistance entry).

fillHoles no longer builds the mean-incident-edge-length and vertex-adjacency tables for all 469k vertices: both take a boolean[] of the vertices the loops will actually read (those with an outgoing boundary edge), so the sqrt and the adjacency writes run for a few hundred vertices instead of 1.4M edges' worth. Neighbour order per vertex is unchanged, so the ring indices and hence the fill output are identical.

orient() scans the edges once instead of three times: the pass that unions consistent components now also records the contested edges' corner slots, orientComponents takes that list instead of re-scanning, and the Mobius count is taken from the contested list alone -- a non-contested edge unions its two faces into one component, so both always take the same flip and can never contradict. splitNonManifold's two edge scans (count non-manifold, then union the manifold fans) are fused into one. The seed order for the component BFS is now one packed (area, face) key per component rather than a sort of all 936k faces; it is the same order, because a component first appears in the descending face order exactly at its largest face.

DE-DUP: UnionFind (new, geometry/mesh/data) holds the disjoint-set forest over a caller-owned int[] parent -- singletons/find/union with path halving. MeshRepair (2 copies), MeshMergeByDistance and MeshSegmenter now all call it; MeshSegmenter's union kept the second root and now keeps the first, which changes only the representative, not the grouping (its only callers are the patch CLI and the segmentation endpoint, which group by root).

DE-DUP: MeshRepair.weld no longer has its own cell-hash weld. It calls MeshMergeByDistance.weld on the input mesh and hands the welder to SlotCarry.weld, which re-indexes corner UVs through sourceFace and tags/bone weights through weldedVertex; readInput then reads the welded bundle. build() records inputVertexCount/inputFaceCount from the pre-weld mesh so the V x->y line still means input to output, and the faces the weld drops as slits are still counted as degenerate deletions.

DE-DUP: MeshRepair and MeshHoleFiller both minted their own packed undirected edge key; both now use the existing EdgeKey (undirected/minVertex/maxVertex), and MeshHoleFiller.undirectedKey plus its KEY_SHIFT/KEY_MASK are deleted. MeshRepair's public cornerEdge field was written on every edge build and read nowhere, so it is gone too -- that alone removed an 11MB allocation, a 2.8M-element fill and 2.8M scattered writes per build.

Line counts: MeshRepair.java 1650 -> 1534, MeshHoleFiller.java 701 -> 684, MeshMergeByDistance -29, MeshSegmenter -16 (net -228 from the files that had the duplication); the shared code it moved to is UnionFind 56, TriangleGeometry 125, TriangleBvh 324. TriangleBvh is new capability rather than moved code -- the containment test it replaces was 60 lines of brute-force scan inside MeshRepair.

Stage order kept: shells are still classified BEFORE the holes are filled, so rays do pass through open loops. Reversing it would fill the boundary loops of the 67 debris shells that are about to be dropped, which changes holeCount and the reported per-hole list -- the report is about the surface that survives. On IMG_4109 the 3-ray majority is unaffected: all 74 loops are small against the shells they sit in, and every containment verdict matches the pre-BVH run exactly.

EVALUATED, not done: moving stages 5-6 onto HalfEdgeMesh after the split. HalfEdgeMeshEngine has no connected-component pass and no boundary-loop walker to reuse -- it offers isBoundaryEdge/isBoundaryHalfEdge/faceAcrossEdge/vertexEdgeAt and nothing above them, and the three boundary walkers that do exist (BridgeEdgeLoopsNode, AdaptiveBridgeLoopsNode, MeshToCurveNode) are private per-node walks with their own semantics (tag groups, polylines). So the move would write the same two loops against a different accessor, delete nothing, and add a full HalfEdgeMesh build in the middle of the pipeline -- assemble's single build already costs ~370ms of the 1.1s, a third of the whole repair. Keeping the flat arrays through stage 6 and building the half-edge mesh once at the end is both less code and much faster.

Verified after the pass: mvn clean compile checkstyle-green; full unit suite 206 tests with only the pre-existing DenseMeshFewSplitsTest '9 to 37' failing; all 11 MeshRepairTest cases green; tools/teavm-build.sh BUILD SUCCESS; the scene reports [repair_mesh] V 468350->469131 F 936035->938302 welded=0 oriented=0 mobius=33 nonManifoldEdges=158 splitVertices=396 degenerate=4 shells=74 dropped=67 holes=74 filled=74 open=0 oversized=0 unfillable=0 boundaryEdges=0 with mesh-state edgeCount 1407453, euler -20, closed=true. Screenshots regenerated at tmp/craw-26-repaired-crawfish.png and tmp/craw-26-repaired-crawfish-back.png.
